scope.flow: reduce-only order matching and Book Open Interest accounting in GTE perpetuals

statements.text: Book OI in each order book's metadata represents the total exposure from pending orders and increases when orders are posted to the book.
Position OI in MarketMetadata tracks the aggregate of all actual user positions.
A reduce-only order is oversized relative to the user's current position, so its excess portion exceeds the current position size.
During order matching, `_matchIncomingOrder` calls `_boundReduceOnlyOrder` when matching against reduce-only orders to ensure the order does not exceed the user's current position.

`_boundReduceOnlyOrder` permanently reduces `ds.metadata.baseOI` or `ds.metadata.quoteOI` by the excess portion immediately upon discovering an oversized reduce-only order, regardless of whether any actual trade occurs, and even when trades execute successfully the Book OI experiences additional reduction beyond what the actual trade should cause.

The excess portion of a reduce-only order represents a mismatch between stale order size and current position size, not real exposure that needs immediate removal, so treating it as exposure to remove causes Book OI to become understated relative to Position OI.
Open Interest should only be adjusted when an actual trade occurs, not during the preparation/bounding phase of order matching.
Book OI should decrease only when orders are filled or removed.
The Position OI and Book OI systems should represent the same underlying economic reality from different perspectives.

ambiguities: Report does not state who submits the oversized reduce-only order or whether any caller restriction applies.
Report does not specify numeric values for the excess portion or the resulting Book OI reduction.
Report does not establish a concrete prior transaction creating the stale order size versus current position mismatch.
